messages:
Megan: Heads-up: Platform wants to standardize client-visible status semantics across routes. Quick sync? We have ambiguous 5xx vs 503 vs 429 usage and console badges are inconsistent.
Sam: Agree. Main pain: SDKs retry behavior expects 5xx=retryable, but we sometimes return 500 for rate-limit-caused failures. Leads to duplicated work and user confusion.
Jia: Proposal: 1) 429 exclusively for rate limits + `Retry-After`. 2) 503 for temporary capacity/backpressure. 3) 5xx/500 for terminal server errors. 4) Add a small machine-readable header `x-rw-status` with category tokens for SDKs.
Omar: Concern: `x-rw-status` needs a stable schema. If we change values mid-rollout it'll break clients. Can we version it like `x-rw-status-v=1` and include an integrity header?
Lucy: From console side, we need a mapping for badge colors and tooltips. Suggest canonical categories: `retryable`, `rate_limited`, `degraded`, `terminal`. Telemetry should emit a `status_category` field in traces so dashboards can aggregate.
Sam: +1. Also need a migration/backfill plan. SDK v2 can read `x-rw-status-v`. For older clients we must preserve legacy semantics (429/5xx). Consider proxy-layer shim that sets `x-rw-status` derived from legacy codes during transition.
Megan: Rollout idea: start internal-only header + alpha SDK. After 2 weeks of sampling (noisy logging) flip a canary proxy rule that maps legacy codes to categories for public endpoints. Add a dashboard that tracks header vs legacy code mismatches and % of traffic using the header.
Jia: Example header formats (draft):
```
x-rw-status: rate_limited
x-rw-status: degraded;reason=overloaded
x-rw-retry-hint: 1s
x-rw-status-v: 1
```
This keeps it simple for SDKs while allowing optional reason metadata.
Omar: Operational note: Dedicated/reserved customers might want different behavior (no auto-retries, different backpressure). We should include `x-rw-tier` or consult route config to expose that. Also document per-route overrides in the rollout playbook.
Lucy: UX copy needs to be short and actionable. Draft tooltips: 
- Rate limit — "Too many requests. Reduce frequency or batch. See quotas."
- Degraded — "Service is throttling due to load. Retry after a short backoff."
- Error — "Unexpected error. Include trace id when contacting support."
Where should the canonical mapping live? I'd prefer a console-managed copy field so we can tweak messaging without code deploys.
Sam: We also need alerting thresholds: if `status_category=degraded` > 1% of traffic over 5m, page SRE; if `rate_limited` spikes, notify product/owners. Telemetry: include route, model, and sample prompt length to help root cause.
Megan: @deploy-bot can we queue a canary job to inject header on 3% traffic? Example command to teams: `kubectl patch deployment api --type='json' -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"INJECT_X_RW_STATUS","value":"true"}}]'`
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: canary header injection to 3% of traffic. Run id: d-20260321-1
Omar: I'll open a PR in infra-config with the spec: header names, versioning, routing exceptions, and per-tenant opt-out. Will include sample responses + integration test stubs.
Megan: Great. Action items: Omar PR + integration tests, Lucy console copy field + dashboard mockups, Jia finalize header spec docs, Sam draft alerting playbook. Collect PRs by EOW and we'll review before canary. Thanks everyone.
